title: Obsolete and Deprecated HTML Features
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of obsolete and deprecated html features in a browser document.
Apply at least one relevant rule from this lesson to a small HTML example.
Check the result using browser inspection, a validator, or an accessibility checklist.

content.intro: This lesson turns “Obsolete and Deprecated HTML Features” into a practical authoring skill. You will work with what obsolete html means, understand the choices that matter, and check the result instead of relying on guesswork.
content.why_it_matters: This topic supports code review and long-term maintenance: recognize old patterns, check current standards, and ship markup whose quality can be explained and tested.

items.title: Checking the current standard before using unfamiliar features
items.text: Checking the current standard before using unfamiliar features is one of the decisions covered by Obsolete and Deprecated HTML Features. Decide what the markup is meant to communicate, choose the native HTML structure that expresses that meaning, and verify the result in a browser or a relevant validation checklist. Avoid using an element or attribute just because its default appearance seems convenient.

content_blocks.title: Keep in mind
content_blocks.text: Prefer the native semantic element that communicates intent. Do not choose markup solely for its default visual style.

content.task: Create a small HTML example that demonstrates obsolete and deprecated html features. Keep the markup minimal, give every element a clear purpose, and inspect the rendered result.
task_acceptance_criteria: Use the relevant concept from Obsolete and Deprecated HTML Features.
Keep IDs unique and use valid nesting.
Check the result in a browser and record one finding.
hints: Start with the smallest valid example for obsolete and deprecated html features.
Add one element or attribute at a time, then check the result.
Compare the source and rendered DOM if the behavior surprises you.

troubleshooting.symptom: The expected content does not appear.
troubleshooting.check: Confirm the file was saved with an .html extension and inspect its path and nesting.
Check the resolved URL and confirm the referenced file or external resource exists and allows the request.

troubleshooting.symptom: The page looks correct but the markup may be invalid.
troubleshooting.check: Run the Nu Html Checker and follow its first relevant diagnostic, then validate again.

common_mistakes.why: The default appearance is not the element’s main meaning and can make navigation or maintenance harder.
common_mistakes.fix: Choose the element that matches the content purpose, then use CSS for presentation.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a browser’s recovery means the source is valid
common_mistakes.why: Browsers often recover from malformed markup, which can hide defects and produce unexpected document structure.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the rendered DOM and run a validator against the original source.

common_mistakes.why: Missing files, narrow viewports, keyboard access, invalid input, or other states can expose defects.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the expected state plus one realistic edge case and an accessibility path.

summary: Obsolete and Deprecated HTML Features is about expressing document structure or behavior intentionally.

Checking the current standard before using unfamiliar features is one of the decisions covered by Obsolete and Deprecated HTML Features. Decide what the markup is meant to communicate, choose the native HTML structure that expresses that meaning, and verify the result in a browser or a relevant validation checklist. Avoid using an element or attribute just because its default appearance seems convenient.
Verify both markup and behavior; do not infer correctness from appearance alone.
